title: coffee.state
description: One coffee, whole, as the catalogue last saw it. Carried in full so that no consumer has to call the producer back.

first_seen_at.description: When this catalogue first saw the coffee. It is not when the roaster released it: for a shop added later the two differ by however long the shop had listed the coffee before a crawl reached it, which can be months. So it means new to this catalogue, not new coffee, and a new-arrivals view built on it has to deal with the hazard that follows. Adding a shop gives its whole catalogue the same first_seen_at, so a hundred coffees from one roaster arrive as new at once and fill a new-arrivals view for a week. A shop that changes its product ids does the same, because every row looks new. The contract cannot tell these apart from genuine arrivals, so a consumer must cap a shop's first crawl or ignore it. Absent or null means the producer did not record it, which says nothing about whether the coffee is old or new.

product_kind.description: What the product is, from the agreed vocabulary. Absent or null means the producer has not decided: that is not beans, and a consumer must not read an undecided product as coffee. other means the producer has decided and the product is none of the named kinds: a decided answer, not a missing one. The list is frozen for this wire version; other is the escape for a kind not yet named, and promoting one to a named kind is a new wire version.

product_kind_source.description: How product_kind was decided, as a sentence. Free text on purpose: it records a method, not a vocabulary.

decaf.description: Whether the shop says the coffee is decaffeinated. There are three answers, not two. true means the shop says it is decaffeinated. false means the shop says it is caffeinated. Absent or null means the shop said nothing about caffeine. Absence is not false: to filter for caffeinated coffee, select false, not anything that is not true, because that sweeps in every page that was silent. This is the same distinction as product_kind, where absence is not a decision.

origin_farm.description: The farm, as the shop names it, free text. Absent or null means the shop names none.

origin_producer.description: The producer, as the shop names it, free text. Absent or null means the shop names none.

origin_washing_station.description: The washing station, as the shop names it, free text. Absent or null means the shop names none.

arabica_pct.description: Share of arabica the shop states, in percent. Null means the shop stated nothing, which is not the same as 0.

robusta_pct.description: Share of robusta the shop states, in percent. Null means the shop stated nothing, which is not the same as 0.

altitude_max_m.description: The upper end of the stated altitude in metres. Equal to altitude_min_m when the shop states a single height. Absent or null means the shop states no altitude.

description.description: The shop's own prose about the coffee, with text the shop repeats across many of its coffees (nutrition tables, FAQs, packaging) already removed by the producer. It is the shop's text, not ours. Absent or null means there is none.

price_minor.description: The price of the package as a count of the minor unit of currency: 34900 is 349.00 when currency is CZK. Null when unpriced.

currency.description: The ISO 4217 code of the currency price_minor is counted in.

price_per_kg_eur_cents.description: The comparable price per kilogram in euro cents: 2450 is 24.50 EUR per kilogram. Null when the shop gives no comparable price.

delisted_at.description: Set once the shop stopped listing it. A delisting is a state rather than a deleted message, so it survives the stream's per-subject compaction.

price_history.description: The coffee's price changes, oldest first, one point per change: a point is emitted only where price_per_kg_eur_cents or available differs from the day before, so a coffee priced the same for a year is one point. The last point holds until observed_at. At most 50 points; a producer trims the oldest before sending, and a longer series is refused. first_seen_at still says when the coffee appeared. Absent and an empty list mean the same thing: the producer recorded no series. Dates must be in strictly ascending order and no two consecutive points may carry the same price and availability; both are checked by the contract's check function, not by this schema.

price_per_kg_eur_cents.description: The comparable price per kilogram in euro cents, a JSON integer as the top-level field is. Null means unpriced that day.

pack_group_key.description: Identifies the same coffee from the same shop in a different pack size: two listings carry the same value exactly when the producer judges them the same coffee from the same shop. It is opaque. Compare it for equality only, and never parse it, order it or rely on its shape. It is not a key for the same coffee across shops, so do not use it to match listings of different shops. Today it looks like <site>/<folded name>, optionally followed by ~espresso or ~filter, for example fathers/uganda zebigi~espresso, and the longest seen is about 132 characters; that is an illustration, not a promise. It contains spaces, / and ~ and non-ASCII characters, so percent-encode it whenever it goes in a URL. Absent or null means the producer could not derive a key, which says nothing about whether other pack sizes exist.
